name: Punjab
summary_text: Pride Amritsar cancelled its 27 April 2025 parade at the Rose Garden after "mounting resistance" from Sikh religious organisations, specifically the Nihang Singh faction and the Akal Takht — the faith's highest temporal authority. Organisers cited religious-group opposition as the reason for cancelling the annual event. Amritsar is the spiritual centre of Sikhism, and the Akal Takht exercises quasi-governmental power over public assembly within its sphere, making this a state-implicated suppression of trans public expression rather than a private dispute. Against the national 0.43, Punjab sits −0.08. While the single-incident rule counsels caution, this event meets the exception: it is state-implicated (a named authority with effective governmental power compelled the cancellation), it was met with impunity (the event simply did not happen), and it directly suppresses the public visibility a visitor relies on for safety. Compared to Delhi (0.38), which also faces police profiling but maintains India's most visible trans civic presence, Punjab's suppression targets the civic presence itself. Compared to Tamil Nadu (0.53), where a court actively commended trans-affirming policy, Punjab demonstrates the inverse dynamic — religious authority vetoing trans assembly. No Punjab-specific welfare board or trans-related statute deviation was identified beyond this event (Punjab is absent from the official 12-board list). The finding is narrow but material: a trans visitor attending a public gathering in Amritsar encounters a documented precedent of institutional suppression.

sources.title: Opposition from religious groups prompts Indian Pride group to cancel annual parade
